name: Modal Verb Frequency
description: Analyzes the frequency and distribution of modal verbs (e.g., 'can', 'could', 'may', 'might', 'must', 'should'). AI models tend to overuse epistemic modals (expressing possibility/necessity) as a stylistic safety mechanism to sound authoritative yet non-committal, avoiding absolute statements.
algorithm: Epistemic and Deontic Modal Density Profiling
mechanism: This algorithm scans the text to extract all modal auxiliary verbs, categorizing them into epistemic (possibility/probability, e.g., 'might', 'seems to', 'could') and deontic (obligation/permission, e.g., 'must', 'should') modalities. The system then calculates the relative frequency of these modals per 1,000 words and compares the distribution against human baselines for the specific document type. Large Language Models (LLMs) are heavily fine-tuned through RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) to be helpful, harmless, and universally objective. Consequently, they structurally avoid making definitive factual assertions that could be construed as hallucinated or biased. Instead, they pad their outputs with a high density of softening modals: 'it is important to consider that...', 'this may indicate...', 'one could argue...'. Human writers, while they do use modals, generally express stronger, more deliberate declarations or opinions. A text exhibiting a mathematically unnatural saturation of non-committal modal verbs strongly indicates the 'safe', hedged output characteristic of AI generation.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing persuasive essays, opinion editorials, and academic writing, differentiating human conviction and definitive research from the overly cautious, hedged tone of an AI.
strengths:
• Directly targets the safety alignment (RLHF) built into modern AI models, which is virtually impossible for the model to bypass without explicit, heavy prompt engineering.
• Highly interpretable and transparent; the evidence (the list of overused modals) can be clearly demonstrated to the user.
• Effective across various languages that utilize clear modal or auxiliary markers for probability/obligation.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when analyzing highly diplomatic human texts, legal disclaimers, or specific academic fields (like theoretical physics) that inherently require cautious, heavily hedged language.
• Short texts might not contain enough verbs to generate a statistically significant modal profile.
• Can be bypassed if a user explicitly prompts the AI to write in an 'aggressive', 'definitive', or 'absolute' tone.
parameters:
Analysis: POS Tagging and Modal Auxiliary Extraction
Metric: Ratio of Modals to Total Verbs and Total Word Count
Output: 0-100 Hedging Saturation (Alignment Safety) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 73-81% accuracy. It is a very reliable indicator of baseline AI tone, though it requires context regarding the intended genre of the text.

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
